region: Eastern Canada and the northeastern and Great Lakes United States
description: Eastern white cedar is a light, soft, aromatic, decay-resistant softwood from eastern North America. It is used for shingles, fencing, log homes, canoes, and outdoor projects.

hazards.summary: IARC classifies all wood dust as carcinogenic to humans, mainly linked to cancer of the nasal cavity and sinuses after long-term heavy exposure. This applies to every species, so dust control matters whatever you cut.

Quebec shingle-mill workers developed asthma from eastern white cedar dust, confirmed by specific inhalation challenge, and plicatic acid (the red cedar asthma agent) was shown to be the cause. About 4 to 7 percent of workers at one sawmill had confirmed occupational asthma.

exposure_limits.note: 8-hour time-weighted average, as restated by OSHA

known_compounds.name: plicatic acid
known_compounds.role: causal agent of asthma; present at roughly half the level found in western red cedar

related_species_note: Cross-reacts with western red cedar (Thuja plicata) through plicatic acid (Cartier-1986). People with red cedar asthma should treat this wood the same way.
image_prompt: Photorealistic studio photograph of a freshly planed eastern white cedar (Thuja occidentalis) board, shot at a low three-quarter angle so the face grain fills most of the frame. Light tan to pale straw-brown heartwood with a faint pinkish cast, and nearly white sapwood along one edge. Straight grain with fine, closely spaced growth rings, a few small dark tight knots, fine even texture, no visible pores, and a soft low luster. Soft diffused daylight from upper left, gentle falloff, neutral warm-grey seamless background, shallow depth of field with the near edge tack-sharp. No text, no logos, no hands, no tools, no finish or varnish, natural unfinished wood. Wide 1200x630 composition (1.91:1) with the board centered and margin on both sides for cropping.
image_alt: Planed board of eastern white cedar with light tan wood, fine straight grain and a few small dark knots.
notes_internal: Not listed in HSE-WIS30. ACGIH TLV for western red cedar (0.5) is species-specific to Thuja plicata; OSHA-CSI does not extend it to Thuja occidentalis, so the general 1 mg/m3 is shown. ACGIH places it in A4 'all other wood dusts' (not named). No dermatitis primary paper found in this pass (Mitchell 1974, PMID 4817210, 'respiratory allergy from Thuja' not reviewed). Absence of reports for a hazard is not evidence that this wood is safe.
